# the contributor audit of the arbitrary-body variance/flux interface

Source: `candidate 7127f9c7b67df7cb`.
Full independent read: **PASS**, with its explicit positive-volume and section-stress hypotheses. This audit replaces reliance on the incorrect pp sign in the older polytopal display.

The actual-fiber hypothesis makes the sampled support heights equal to their finite concave roof at every sampled base. The finite linear-programming dual has an attained optimal majorant; its pointed optimal face has a vertex, determined by an affine basis of sampled bases. There are finitely many such bases. Their interpolation coefficients are continuous bounded functions of the continuous unit normal, so choosing the first feasible touching interpolant gives a bounded Borel selector. This construction works in the affine span of the base, including dimension zero. It does not change the lattice or require an ambient facet.

The martingale row stays on the selected exposed support plane by nonnegativity of its gap and zero conditional mean. Testing with bounded Borel functions of the selected label avoids an uncountable-null-set argument. Disintegrating by that label preserves the row-barycenter tests, including the quadratic cross-term tests. Thus the covariance difference is exactly the actual increment variance and has the asserted support-plane kernel. Target ownership is correctly retained as a transport-induced kernel, rather than identified with the source selector.

Fiber Gauss--Green follows from coordinate-line integration and the area formula for convex boundary graphs. Its use for the two polynomial fields requires no approximation. At a proper cap the new boundary has outward normal -v, so cap flux equals its allocated body flux MINUS section flux. At inside and outside supporting coincidences the respective identities alpha+sigma=1 and alpha=sigma give the full-body and zero-volume contributions exactly. This includes d=1 and arbitrary admissible fractional allocations.

Subtracting weighted cap flux from full-body flux therefore gives a PLUS raw section term. Expanding that term at its actual section centroid gives MINUS its pp covariance times the integer normal. Consequently the corrected pp identity has two negative covariance sums. The xx identity is unchanged: both intermediate mixed blocks have minus signs, and the two support-plane kernels turn them into positive xx-normal terms. All integrals are finite because the selected support coefficients, physical set, and covariance fields are bounded.

The three equal-interval certificate satisfies all displayed hypotheses, including genuine global criticality, common section centroids and the identity boundary coupling. Direct integration gives pp discrepancy -1/2 and cap covariance contribution -(2)(1/4)=-1/2. The old plus sign would give the opposite value. Its xx discrepancy and section covariance both equal 1/8. This is a decisive geometric sign certificate, not an arbitrary matrix example.

The extension removes the polytopal restriction from this necessary-condition interface. It does not establish the assumed section-stress identities for arbitrary cap selections, does not cover lower-dimensional fibers by fiat, and does not infer a common sign from covariance positivity. The quantitative common-center step of OC remains absent.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
